Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Reversals of previous rulings and new errata contained herein go into
effect for V:EKN Constructed Tournaments on May 31, 2002.

CARD-SPECIFIC CLARIFICATIONS, RULINGS, AND ERRATA:

CLARIFICATIONS:

MALLEABLE VISAGE doesn't change the acting minion. The original acting
ally is still the actor. Since he was blocked (a requirement for playing
Malleable Visage), the No Repeat Actions rule (if it is being used) would
restrict him from performing the same action again this turn.

RULINGS:

EAGLE'S SIGHT won't change a Methuselah's "I don't block" decision. It
allows a non-target Methuselah to block directed action, and allows a
Methuselah other than the predator or prey to block an undirected action.
It won't overcome any other obstacle to blocking (like stealth,
Seduction, Day Operation, or a prior "I don't block" decision).
(REVERSAL)

If a vampire bleeds with FORCE OF WILL and the bleed action is canceled
(via Change of Target, for example), then the acting vampire doesn't
suffer the aggravated damage, since there is no combat.

KHOBAR TOWERS will take X as the blood cost or pool cost of an ally.
(REVERSAL)

The untap effect of MAJESTY (and Earth Meld and Meld with the Land)
occurs when the strike resolves (it is not delayed until after combat
ends).

If a vampire is stolen via SPIRIT MARIONETTE and then bleeds (as required)
and the bleed action is canceled (via Change of Target, for example), the
vampire still returns to its original controller, since that "next
action" (the bleed that was canceled) is over. (REVERSAL)

ERRATA:

THE GRANDEST TRICK makes vampires unable to block the minion who played
it, not the action in general (so if it is Masked, vampires can attempt
to block the new acting vampire).

MELANGE should refer to the "minion with this card" not "the vampire with
this card" - it still functions when played on an acting ally.

PSYCHOMACHIA is playable when an ally or younger vampire blocks
(successfully) - not merely on the attempt. (So the NRA rule, if used,
would "kick in" to prevent the vampire from attempting the same type of
action again).

GENERAL RULINGS:

For allies that are able to play certain cards "as a vampire", they are
treated as vampires for all parts of the resolution of the play of the
appropriate cards. This includes the resolution of an action card and the
resolution of a strike card. It does not include any continuing effects
granted by the card (after its resolution) nor any effects given by a
card in play. This reverses a few previous rulings regarding the
resolution of, for example, Burst of Sunlight (will harm the ally
striking "as a vampire") and the ability of an ally to use Charming Lobby
to call a vote (allowed if the ally plays Charming Lobby "as a vampire").
(REVERSAL)

Effects that end combat and then do something else after combat (all in the
single resolution of the effect) will fizzle if combat doesn't end or if a
new combat is started. (Changes: Rotschreck followed by Fast Reaction or
Psyche! will nullify the torpor effect.) Note that this doesn't apply to
end combat and untap effects - the untap effect is not delayed to after
combat (see Majesty ruling above).

If an effect resolves and sets up an effect to be resolved later (e.g.,
Undead Persistence's torpor effect or Siren's Lure's combat), then the
effect will not be canceled by "interruptions" (extending combat/starting
combat/etc.).

An effect which would cause (a new) combat cannot be used if there is
already a "to be resolved later" combat.

Some cards grant a minion the option of doing something and then go on to
say that some other effect will occur "if he does so". The second effect
is only applied if the minion uses the effect (the first effect) provided
by the card. If he does the effect, but doesn't use the card (i.e., he has
some additional ability which allows him to do the same effect), then the
secondary effect of the card doesn't occur. That is, "if he does so" means
"if he uses this card's effect to do so". For example, Ian Forestal with
an Infernal Familiar can play a card that requires, say, Necromancy (a
Discipline he doesn't have) as if he had basic Necromancy. This ability
is granted separately by both his own card text and the text on the
Infernal Familiar. If he plays a card that requires Necromancy via the
Familiar ("if he does so"), then the Infernal Familiar gets an additional
investment counter, by card text. If he uses his special ability to play
such a card, the Familiar doesn't. (REVERSAL)

Why was this necessary? It made the card interesting that it

with this errata, the Presence ability is worse than Change of
Target (on two counts: one, it costs blood, and two, you have
to have been blocked by an ally or younger vampire). (The only
advantage [pre] Psychomachia has over Change of Target now is
that if you're *not* using NRA you're not under same-action

Designer intent? If so, I wish the designer had intended it

Hmmm. I thought Curt Adams' suggestion was much better - that
allies should *never* have anything applied to them that's only
supposed to apply to vampires, because when they have these
abilities, it's only supposed to mean that they can do some things
that vampires do, not that they *are* in any way vampires. So
Burst of Sunlight should never do damage to an ally; an ally
should never be able to call a vote (that requires a vampire to
call); an ally should never be able to benefit from Ex Nihilo
(the last one is still true). :-)

> Effects that end combat and then do something else after combat (all in
the

> Psyche! will nullify the torpor effect.) Note that this doesn't apply to

Oy. Why was this necessary? I can see the logic behind "if
combat doesn't end" but "if a new combat is started" has no
obvious reason to dissolve these effects. The first combat
ended; things that happen "after that combat" can happen; a
new combat can begin.

I don't understand how Rotschreck can be nullified, either;
don't all its effects - including the torporization - get
applied before anyone becomes eligible to play Psyche! or
Fast Reaction? And once that's happened, there's no opposing
vampire eligible to be Psyche!d against. (Fast Reaction
could still be playable if it was the blocking vampire that
was the Rotschreck victim, but again I don't see why a Fast
Reaction being played after resolution of Rotschreck should
retroactively cancel Rotschreck's effects.)

There are two major things, in my mind, that have made this game
great. The first is its' intuitive, logical design. V:tes is
relatively easy to grasp, yet complex enough to allow nearly endless
variety in games. The second is the story. I think that all will agree
that this game could not have come nearly as far as it has without the
roleplaying element. The key to game design, as far as i am concerned,
is maintaining a comfortable balance between these two necessary
things. In many cases, if the story were allowed to be compromised,
our game would benefit in becoming a more logical process, but less
people would be interested in playing. And sometimes, in an effort to
be more forthright with the rules, we tread on certain story aspects.

roleplaying inconsistencies, when rules are easily clarified in other
ways. For example, a scenario where a Rafastio ghoul is being removed
from the game by exposure to sunlight invites ridicule. I always
thought that when an ally says 'may use tha/pot/pre as a vampire' what
it meant was 'may use tha/pot/pre as a vampire (would)', not 'may use
tha/pot/pre as if it were a vampire'. The distinction is slight, but
it's enough to rend holes in the storyline's credibility. Under the
first reading of the card, the ghoul would not need to go to torpor.

players, I think that it is important to maintain the integrity of the
roleplaying backstory -- every bit as important as simplifying and
clarifying the rules.

It actually seems like there is now. If the ally plays a discipline
card, thereby becoming "like a vampire" and subject to vampire
frailities (such as vulnerability to aggravated damage), it should
also be vulnerable to a Rotschreck if the opposing minion is able play
one and send the ally (vampire wannabe due to a discipline card it
played) into torpor. It would then revert back to ally status.
However, as there is no mechanism to rescuing allies in torpor within
the rules, they would have to stay there indefinitely. It could then
bring up the question of bloodhunts on vampires snacking on torporized
allies? But this is all conjecture as you stated in an earlier post
that torporize allies would burn, however, you also then stated
afterward that it didn't really require an input into the rules. Why
not? I can not see any leap of logic that would lead me into that
direction. Especially as allies, per the rules, treat aggravated
damage as normal damage and die when they reach zero life.

What does disturb me is trying to explain this to new players without
turning them off from the game. Right now house rules here follow
tournament rules to allow any new (and current) players to build and
play decks that can then be picked up and played at any sanctioned
tournament anywhere. If this ruling makes my head hurt, what do you
think it will do to new players? And I do not think giving aspirin
will solve the problem while introducing this new ruling.

I sincerely believe that allies, following the last printed rules
currently available to players worldwide (Final Nights), should be
immune to aggravated damage, period. Players with allies wanting to
play discipline cards that indicate a vampire as only being able to
play it should not be allowed to play the cards. Why? Card text
states only vampires can play the card. It doesn't matter if it is a
discipline card or not, otherwise all V:TES discipline cards should
indicate "only useable by a vampire". They don't and therefore
certain discipline cards are available to allies to use provided they
have text stating they may use cards requiring disciplines. Besides
only vampires can normally use discipline cards and they are the only
minions who can receive discipline cards during Master phases. Allies
brought out with discipline cards do not fall under this as their card
text specifically states otherwise.

As it stands now, if an ally comes out that can use Obtenebration, it
could effectively use Black Metamorphosis and become a vampire from
then on as it could play the card "as a vampire" and then remain so as
card text could lead one to believe.

But then again, I have always understood the text "may play
(discipline) cards as if a vampire with a capacity of #" to mean the
ally has a set blood/life expenditure level on whatever discipline
card it wants to play no matter how much life it actually has.

Yes, a Shadow Court Satyr could be brought out and then receive a
Burst of Sunlight combat card to make it a real bad MF, but it is
still an ally and should have different vulnerabilities. The worse
vulnerability has always been pool cost for a recruited minion that is
more perishable than your average vampire. Too much normal damage on
vampire = naptime in your local torpor flowergarden. Too much normal
damage on an ally = death.

The new ruling on interrupting card effects also does not set will. I
can see the possibility of Psyche! performing the interrupt against
Rotschreck as it is a combat card, I do not see it with Fast Reaction.

Fast Reaction is a reaction card and must wait until after the combat
has ended before play. If a diablerie and bloodhunt are tied to each
other, then cards played within combat that have effects outside of
the combat should have priority over new cards trying to get into the
mix. Psyche! can possibly bypass this due to it being a combat card
and therefore being able to legally enter the card mix during combat.
Fast Reaction is a different class of card, reaction not combat.

However, I do not see any timing identified within combat when a
vampire is placed into torpor (either before combat ends or after
combat ends). If you go by order of card text, then you prescribe an
order where combat ends and the vampire is sent to torpor. But after
looking at that, the intuitive aspect of a player should be to
complete one card prior to implementing another. If that would be the
case, then Psyche! would also fail to interrupt a Rotschreck as
neither one of the two minions would be ready.

Michael Eichler

bypass this restriction. Charming Lobby text reads - "+1 stealth
political action. Call a referendum. If the referendum passes, then
the next referendum called thereafter passes automatically. (S) As
above, and this vampire gains 2 votes for the first referendum."
If allies can not call referendums in the rules and the card text
specifically states "Call a referendum", are you telling me that
enables bypasss capability?
How? The logic does not stand up to scrutiny.

Now back to the sentence - play basic (discipline) cards as if a
vampire with a capacity of (some number). I can understand there
being some cards that restrict usage based upon capacity level. An
example could be Precognizant Mobility if an ally was able to play
basic Auspex cards as a vampire with a capacity of 3. This would mean
that the ally could untap another vampire or ally that either had a
capacity of 2 or less, or a cost of 2 or less. However, I do not see
the justification of just taking the fragment "as a vampire"
constitutes your new ruling based upon current text. Now if an ally
with this sentence - ally may play basic (discipline) cards as a
vampire; I would then understand the reasoning to bring out a ruling
as you have presented. But just to take something out of context and
making a ruling on it, is a mistake.

I have also viewed the sentence - play basic (discipline) cards as if
a vampire with a capacity of (some number) - to also represent an
upper limit as to the amount of life that ally could expend within one
turn where it might use more than one allowable discipline card that
had blood costs. And to also set the upper limit on any one allowable
discipline card the ally could use overall. Example would be - Shadow
Court Satyr. It has the sentence "may only use the basic ability of a
discipline card as a vampire with a capacity of 1. Therefore it could
not be brought out with a Decapitate as it requires 2 blood and the
Saytr can only play discipline cards as a vampire with a capacity of
1.

Please show me where this does not follow a logical order based upon
the complete sentence.

Otherwise, why would you have allies that could use some basic
disipline cards as a vampire with a capacity of varying numbers? Why
not just make them all the same? Instead you have different numbers
to restrict the amount of life an ally and expend in one turn and to
restrict it from using certain basic discipline cards that do not
explictly state that the card is only useable by a vampire.

<snip>

> Ex Nihilo and Rutor's Hand are the usual examples (since allies
> currently exist to play these cards).
>

Oh... So allies now have the capability to play cards that are
reserved for vampires only. This does not meet the "press to test"
button criteria. An ally is not a vampire. Whatever happened to just
following card text? Rutor's Hand has the following sentence in it
that logically excludes allies from playing it - "Put this card on the
acting vampire". If you were to follow that direction of thought, you
would see that while allies may have the capability to play basic
discipline card as a vampire with some kind of capacity level, it does
not in fact make them vampires. It just means they have access to
cards not normally allowed to allies as a whole.

> > But then again, I have always understood the text "may play
> > (discipline) cards as if a vampire with a capacity of #" to mean the
> > ally has a set blood/life expenditure level on whatever discipline
> > card it wants to play no matter how much life it actually has.
>
> No. It doesn't mean that at all.
>

Why? I don't follow the reasoning as to why they shouldn't.

> The capacity level is set because some cards that require disciplines
> refer to the capacity of the vampire playing it (since all such cards
> are written under the assumption that they will be played by vampires,
> per the rules).

Really? Where in the rules does it state that? If it is due to the
"As a vampire" fragment that is being taken out of context, then the
logic is flawed.

>
> > The new ruling on interrupting card effects also does not set will. I
> > can see the possibility of Psyche! performing the interrupt against
> > Rotschreck as it is a combat card, I do not see it with Fast Reaction.
> >
> > Fast Reaction is a reaction card and must wait until after the combat
> > has ended before play. If a diablerie and bloodhunt are tied to each
> > other, then cards played within combat that have effects outside of
> > the combat should have priority over new cards trying to get into the
> > mix.
>
> That "If ... then ..." is not valid.
>
> Form of Mist has long been thwarted by Fast Reaction.
>

I never said anything against Fast Reaction vs Form of Mist. Form of
Mist allows you to continue the action which in turn allows reaction
cards to come to the forefront. Fast Reaction text has specific
provisions that allow the initiation of another combat without the
need to re-intercept.

> > Psyche! can possibly bypass this due to it being a combat card
> > and therefore being able to legally enter the card mix during combat.
> > Fast Reaction is a different class of card, reaction not combat.
> >
> > However, I do not see any timing identified within combat when a
> > vampire is placed into torpor (either before combat ends or after
> > combat ends). If you go by order of card text, then you prescribe an
> > order where combat ends and the vampire is sent to torpor. But after
> > looking at that, the intuitive aspect of a player should be to
> > complete one card prior to implementing another. If that would be the
> > case, then Psyche! would also fail to interrupt a Rotschreck as
> > neither one of the two minions would be ready.
>
> Sure. And if that (perfectly plausible) ruling were made, then
> Telepathic Counter couldn't interrupt a Catatonic Fear, for example.
>

Again Telepathic Tracking at superior has text containing specific
provisions to allow the interruption of Catatonic Fear as it is a
combat card being used in a combat. Catatonic Fear (at superior) is a
S:CE with and after combat effect. Telepathic Tracking (at superior)
prevents the ending of combat and moves it to the start of the next
round.

> With the various interractions weighed, the current ruling was
> deemed to be the least troublesome.

I do not see how. If you use the above reasoning I have with
discipline using allies, I see no problems whatsoever. With the Fast
Reaction overriding Rotschreck, I do not see logical flow for allowing
Fast Reaction to preimpt a vampire from going to torpor. I really
don't even see it, after some thought, with Psyche! as the combat ends
because one of the minions is sent to torpor. Which would seem to
follow the logical order of combat ending in an aggravated damage
First Strike sending an opposing vampire to torpor and ending combat
before the other player has the chance to play anything else.
Psyche!, while a combat card, requires both minions to be ready to
enable it's use. If one is sent to torpor then it is no longer ready
and does not follow the dictates of the card text.

No matter what the case, a combat can only exist between two ready
minions and if one is no longer ready then you no longer have a
combat.

But I can see with some cards like Amaranth being tossed out to
counter what I have above and again, all I can say is look at the card
text. It specifically states "Play when the opposing vampire is going
to torpor". Fast Reaction and Psyche! do not.

opponent, Smudge, plays Dodge! as his strike (ghoul = acting minion).

torpor. However, at this point, the ghoul isn't doing anything that
relates to BoS. So, he shouldn't be a vampire at this point. And
thus, when fails to prevent the damage, he just burns the blood.What's
wrong with that?

regarding allies with disciplines, at least with the intent of his
statement. I like attributing the 'vampireness' to the card, and not
the Ally. And since it is now clear the matter is going back to RT
review, I wish to add something that might be constructive, hopefully.

were playing it" still means the Rafaisto will get hit with 1 agg
himself, since he would be the vampire that the card would be "as if
played by". Using the second suggestion ("as a vampire of capacity Y
[would play it]") still leaves an ally vulnerable, if I interpret
things correctly.

(I know the previous sentences are horrible, but to my dismay I cannot
find an easy way to say it in a clearer fashion right now. It's almost
as bad as time-travel and the Hitchhiker's Guide.)

What might work is something like:

"The ally may play cards requiring X by paying an amount of life equal
to its blood cost, with a maximum of Y. Any blood gained or lost is
considered to be life. (Text on the played card referring to 'this
(acting) vampire' refers to 'this (acting) minion'. Mandatory effects
that result from the card being played also occur.)"

If it were desired that a capacity be attached to this action or
combat card, (with regards to effects such as obedience, or 'younger'
etc.) a line could be added in the manner of: "cards that refer to a
(base) capacity use a value of Z."

I'm not really sure I'm helping out here, unfortunately. Maybe it'll
spark an idea somewhere.

I believe this rule is a result of how Psyche has to work to
work at all. It's a combat card, so you have to play it "in
combat". But combat has to have ended for it to be playable
(at superior). So it "has to" work as a sort of interrupt,
played "while" combat is ending as a result of some other
card's effect (or when combat ends "normally").

Given that Psyche works against Strike: Combat Ends - *after*
the S:CE resolves - it sort of makes sense that it can also
"interrupt" Rotschreck's "end combat" instruction, since we
have no reason to assume that Rotschreck produces a "stronger"
combat-ending effect than S:CE does.

I personally would prefer that the play/resolution of any
one card not be interruptable at all (ie all of Rotschreck
would happen "atomically" and once it was done Psyche wouldn't
be playable) but since S:CE already essentially requires
Psyche to work as an interrupt, I can see the reasoning behind
it. I think.

It's not obvious to me why "untap" effects should be exempt
from being "after combat" either, though.

better model of the RPG mechanics, as well as reduce confusion/inconsistency

Rotschreck: Master: out-of-turn. Play when a minion attempts to use an
aggravated damage (strike?) against a vampire that is effective at the current
range. The opposing vampire (vampire opposing the striking vampire?) **goes to
torpor**, tapped, with this card on it before damage is resolved. During the
vampire's next untap phase, burn this card instead of untapping the vampire.

end** (with no uncancelled press to continue). Enter combat with the opposing

minion. This is a new combat.

desirable than a ruling) eliminate the opportunity for Psyche & TT to interrupt

unsure how this would change the resolution of any "S:CE and..." strikes.

(nor do I really care).

Feedback requested from interested parties. :)

If you are allowed to play one effect while another is resolving (and this
wasn't explicitly ruled to be a new allowance, only for cards that are played
at the end of combat, but the ruling about playing Psyche! during Rotschreck
seemed to *assume* that you could interrupt effects with other effects), then
why not play a Bonding in between the untap effect of 2nd Tradition and the
intercept effect of it? Or how about cards that say, "choose a vampire" and
then do something to that vampire. Why not play an effect after the vampire is
chosen, but nothing has happened to him?

Now, granted, that usually wouldn't mean anything. The ruling said that
effects that end combat and do something else will lose the "something else" if
combat is restarted. They said nothing about interrupting an effect and
causing all other effects to be lost. So up to here, the point would be moot.
However, in your continually inarticulate explanation of the LfD/BBA ruling,
you implied that any effect that interrupted currently resolving effects would
cause additional effects to be lost (don't ask me to clarify that... it
doesn't seem to make much sense, but you said it, not me). If this is the
case, then you could "counterspell" any multi-effect card by playing effects in
the middle of it. Playing a bleed modifier after 2nd Tradition has untapped
you but before you have gained the intercept (or after the intercept but before
the untap, depending on what order it goes in), would then cancel the rest of
the card.

Certainly that can't be the case. We all know that's not the way the game
works, and I assume you're not trying to change it to be like that, but it
seems to be what you have implied. The rulings cited only make sense in such a
context.
